children: In Phase 2 SOLSTICE, 28/28 patients completing 96 weeks of combination therapy had undetectable viremia. In an exploratory analysis, all 10 patients who discontinued treatment achieved SVR12; follow-up ranged from 12 to 48 weeks and remains ongoing.
All patients completing 96 weeks of combination therapy reached the reported virologic endpoint; no prior-period comparison was provided.
An early signal for treatment-free viral control, but the analysis is exploratory, preliminary and based on 10 patients.
Longer follow-up is limited, and the release says all 10 patients are continuing follow-up.
No viral rebound or ALT flares observed
No events were observed in these 10 patients so far; follow-up is incomplete and safety data have not been fully assessed.
The planned filing is a future milestone, subject to the company’s development and regulatory plans.

These results extend Phase 2 evidence for Vir Biotechnology’s investigational hepatitis delta combination and include an early, small-sample treatment-discontinuation analysis. Further follow-up of discontinuers and the ECLIPSE registrational program, including the announced ECLIPSE 1 topline results, will be important to assess durability and support the planned mid-2027 U.S. FDA filing.
